data.title: U.K. Retail Sales Resilience Unlikely to Last — Market Talk
data.description: Retail sales held up well in October, but this momentum is expected to slow going forward, Paul Dales at Capital Economics says in a note. Sales rose 0.7% on the month, supported by a pickup in clothing and food sales. However, this reflected a bump from seasonal weather given retailers' new autumn and winter ranges, Dales says. "And the 0.8% rise in food sales might not be so strong in the coming months since some of it was due to household 'prepping' by buying UHT [milk] and tinned goods." Spending at this level is unlikely to continue with consumer confidence low and utilities prices set to jump in January. "We doubt that the continued resilience of real retail spending in October can last." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

data.title: Nasdaq Set for Fresh Decline as AI Selloff Intensifies
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.15%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to more than 17%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, fell more than 5% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks opened 3% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.2% lower.

Demand for Anthropic's IPO is focusing attention on the sustainability of the AI investment buildout while also draining liquidity from the broader market, said Roger Lee, head of equity strategy at Cavendish.

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 1.25% to $90.85 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 1.7% to trade around $81.80 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 6 basis points to 4.720%. Thirty-year yields fell 3.1 basis points to trade around 5.370%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling close to 3% at $3,580 a troy ounce. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin rebounded slightly but remained near July lows, hovering just below $62,000.

For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.

data.title: Diesel markets recover slightly; east-west remains supportive for jet fuel
data.description:
Asia's diesel market focus for the week was on fresh December refiner sales and term negotiations for next year, while jet fuel's bright spot came from the east-west arbitrage window.

Refiners were clearing their December spot cargoes at discounts of $2-3 a barrel to benchmark Singapore prices, against a backdrop of sufficient supplies, especially in northeast Asia.

Overall slow regional demand entering the year-end is also contributing to the weaker trading sentiment.

Refining margins (GO10SGCKMc1) rebounded from the previous session and were back at $53 a barrel, though they remain $7 lower week-on-week.

Cash differentials (GO10-SIN-DIF) recovered to a premium of 4 cents a barrel, though these levels were still one-third of last week's close.

For jet fuel, the focus was on whether more cargoes could heat west, with the arbitrage window open both to Europe and the US West Coast.

Deals for northeast Asian barrels this week were done at premiums linked to benchmark Singapore quotes, with cash differentials (JET-SIN-DIF) flipping into a premium for the first time in nearly a month.

Traders were still hoping for the emergence of heating demand to partially bolster kerosene buying interest, which could, in turn, support jet fuel demand.

Regrade (JETREG10SGMc1) continued trading at slight discounts.

SINGAPORE CASH DEALS

- No deal for gasoil or jet fuel

INVENTORIES

- Gasoil stocks slipped 1.3% on the week to 1.762 million tons, down 19.2% on the year. Wageningen said import volumes remained high, but outflows were also strong, including shipments to Brazil, while inland demand continued to improve.

NEWS

- Restarting a shuttered refinery near Houston, Texas, will be a costly test of President Donald Trump's agenda to boost US fuel output as prices surge amid a global supply squeeze, with analysts estimating the total price tag could reach $1 billion.

- Russia's crude oil output risks falling again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say.

- Oil prices edged down on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

data.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Gulf Exports Recover — Market Talk
data.description: Oil prices retreat after earlier gains as traders assess improving global supply conditions and continued threats to Middle Eastern shipments. Brent crude falls 0.9% to $91.18 a barrel, while WTI declines 0.8% to $82.56. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that increasing oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have contributed to the recent decline in crude prices. The agency expects global inventories to build as Middle Eastern production and exports recover, while demand remains relatively flat in the near term. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

data.title: European Shares Extend Losses For Fifth Day On AI Jitters
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks traded lower for a fifth consecutive session on Friday and headed for their worst weekly drop since March due to ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence and chip stocks.

Anthropic's record listing in New York failed to stem concerns over slower AI infrastructure spending and rising debt loads in the sector.

The British pound was under pressure, holding at its lowest level in almost a year against the dollar, despite the release of improved U.K. retail sales and consumer confidence data.

U.K. retail sales increased 0.7 percent in October from September as consumers stocked up on long-life food items following the government's Be Ready campaign launch.

GfK's consumer sentiment index rose to -22 in November from -24 in October as shoppers became more willing to make big-ticket purchases ahead of Christmas.

Eurozone consumer confidence figures, final U.S. consumer sentiment data and comments from Fed and ECB officials will be in the spotlight as the day progresses.

The pan-European STOXX 600 dopped 0.9 percent to 632.45 after falling 0.9 percent on Thursday to reach its lowest level in nearly four weeks. For the week, the index was down nearly 4.5 percent, marking its steepest decline since March.

The German DAX tumbled 1.3 percent, France's CAC 40 shed 0.9 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down half a percent.

Tech stocks such as ASML Holding, STMicroelectronics and Aixtron plummeted 5-8 percent on concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom.

Drax shares fell 1.3 percent in London after the energy firm agreed to acquire Bluefield Services Ltd. and certain of its subsidiaries for 9.15 million pounds.

Oslo-headquartered Hunter Group fell nearly 2 percent after launching a NOK1.63bn ($168m) takeover bid for Norwegian offshore accommodation specialist Jacktel.

French construction company Vinci was little changed after bagging a contract to build an LNG tank in Canada.

data.title: China's Industrial Profit Likely Remained Weak in October — Market Talk
data.description:
0933 GMT - China's industrial profits likely remained weak in October, according to ING in a research note. While companies' profits have generally recovered in 2026, the rebound remains uneven, it says. Gains have been concentrated in AI and electronics-related industries and upstream commodity producers, it notes. Automakers, construction-linked sectors, and many consumer-facing manufacturers continue to face significant pressure, it adds. Soft domestic demand is likely to keep these sectors under pressure in the October data, ING says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)

0931 GMT - Retail sales held up well in October, but this momentum is expected to slow going forward, Paul Dales at Capital Economics says in a note. Sales rose 0.7% on the month, supported by a pickup in clothing and food sales. However, this reflected a bump from seasonal weather given retailers' new autumn and winter ranges, Dales says. "And the 0.8% rise in food sales might not be so strong in the coming months since some of it was due to household 'prepping' by buying UHT [milk] and tinned goods." Spending at this level is unlikely to continue with consumer confidence low and utilities prices set to jump in January. "We doubt that the continued resilience of real retail spending in October can last." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

0855 GMT - The U.K. and EU are expected to announce new agreements that will improve British trade on Friday but sterling is unlikely to rise much in response, ING's Chris Turner writes in a note. "Sterling typically responds well to the prospect of closer U.K. ties with Europe on the view that reversing a bad Brexit deal can generate a 1-2% larger U.K. economy in 5-10 years time." Today's agreements are fully expected, however, and might not strengthen sterling, he says. Sterling could rise if Bank of England tightening expectations prove more resilient than those for the European Central Bank, the analyst adds. The euro falls 0.1% to 0.8369 pounds and ING expects to end the year at 0.8300 pounds. Sterling rises 0.2% to $1.3107. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0847 GMT - Bitcoin and ether trade higher in early European trade, but fail to recover losses after heavy selling in the last session. A global tech selloff bled across other risk assets, Deutsche Bank analysts write, pushing bitcoin down to around $61,500--more than 29% lower than its September peak. The cryptocurrency trades at its lowest level since early July. Investor expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening also weigh on nonyielding digital assets. Bitcoin adds 0.8% to trade at $61,961, while ether gains 0.85% to trade at $1,754.(josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

0831 GMT - Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, fall as investors move funds from risk assets such as stocks to safer assets like government bonds. Fears about a possible slowdown in the AI industry are driving risk-off sentiment. Meanwhile the latest U.K. public finances data show borrowing in October came in at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion), while the borrowing estimate for the financial year to September was revised down by 3.6 billion pounds, to 94.3 billion pounds. Ten-year gilt yields fall 1.7 basis points to last trade at 5.298%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0821 GMT - The Hungarian forint remains under pressure after reaching a seven-month low against the euro overnight on the prospect of the National Bank of Hungary cutting interest rates and risk aversion. The NBH held rates at 5.5% earlier this week but signaled room for monetary easing. The currency is also under pressure due to an unwinding of carry trades, which involve borrowing in a low-yielding currency to invest in a currency with higher yields, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. The euro rises 0.5% to 372.83 forints after reaching as high as 373.57 overnight. "Any euro-forint close above the 373.65 upside gap from April would warn of an extension to 380," Turner says. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0816 GMT - U.K. public finances remain stretched, which could challenge the government's ability to maintain its fiscal rules, Pantheon Macroeconomics' Rob Wood and Elliott Jordan-Doak say in a note. The latest data show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds ($22 billion) in October, a 5.2% increase from a year ago. The October budget failed to address the main challenges facing U.K. finances, meaning the fiscal position could deteriorate further, the economists say. "We continue to have doubts about the government's ability to follow through on its fiscal plans, suggesting upside risks to borrowing in the coming years." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0747 GMT - Sterling briefly edges higher after U.K. retail sales showed a rebound in October. Retail sales rose 0.7% on month, data from the Office for National Statistics show. The reading went against a consensus forecast of flat growth and came after a downwardly revised 0.6% decline in September. The ONS separately reports that public sector net borrowing in October was 17 billion pounds, better than the 18 billion pounds expected. Sterling initially rises to an intraday high of $1.3123 from $1.3115 before the data's release. The euro last trades at 0.8376 pounds, little changed from levels before the data, after briefly falling to an intraday low of 0.8370. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0741 GMT - U.K. retail sales data for October came in better than the September data, indicating that economic activity remains resilient, Omnis Investments' Patrick O'Donnell says in a note. Monthly retail sales rose 0.7% in October, following a 0.6% fall in September. "Whilst there is some evidence of a drag on real spending from rising fuel and utility prices and higher borrowing costs, the economy continues to hold up overall." (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0739 GMT - High borrowing costs on U.K. government bonds could continue to weaken public finances, Quilter's Kit Rees says in a note. Public sector finance data released on Friday show public borrowing stood at 17 billion pounds [$22 billion] in October, up 5.2% from the same period a year ago. Higher debt interest costs largely contributed to the increase. "Borrowing costs remain elevated and with further hiking from the Bank of England to come, the government is going to find itself increasingly hemmed in by the cost of its debt," Rees says. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0719 GMT - The dollar edges lower after Anthropic's record-breaking initial public offering failed to halt selling in U.S. AI-related stocks overnight. However, the dollar's pullback is modest, remaining near the 19-month high reached Thursday, supported by expectations for further interest-rate rises by the Federal Reserve. "As the global business cycle begins to lose momentum, we see the U.S. economy on a relatively stronger footing, and the solid domestic demand will allow the Fed to extend its hiking cycle further than peers," says Danske Bank's Kirstine Kundby-Nielsen in a note. The DXY dollar index is down 0.2% at 103.738, having reached 103.974 Thursday, its highest level since April 2025. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0712 GMT - Malaysia's export performance is expected to remain supported by resilient electrical and electronics shipments, alongside sustained demand for commodity-related products, particularly LNG and petroleum products, RHB senior economist Chin Yee Sian says in a note. The global technology growth cycle, driven by artificial-intelligence adoption and data-center investment, should support semiconductor demand, she says. Other manufactured exports, including chemicals, machinery and metal products, could also benefit from regional production and infrastructure spending, she reckons. However, a slowdown in AI-related investment, tighter U.S. chip controls and prolonged geopolitical disruptions could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

data.title: SK Hynix to become top shareholder in rival Kioxia after bond conversion
data.description:
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix Inc will become the largest shareholder in Japanese rival Kioxia Holdings by converting bonds of an investment vehicle into shares in December.

SK Hynix said it would convert the bonds into 129,000 common shares and buy 1,001 additional shares in the entity from Bain Capital, a transaction that will give SK Hynix an indirect stake of about 14.1% in Kioxia.

SK Hynix also said it had no current plans to buy or sell additional Kioxia shares and its participation in Kioxia's management would remain limited after the deal.

The plan comes amid robust demand for NAND chips, used for storage in devices ranging from smartphones to servers in AI data centers.

SK Hynix is the No.2 maker of NAND chips, with a 19% share, while Kioxia ranks fourth with a 14% share, according to research firm Counterpoint.

In 2018, SK Hynix invested a total of 395 billion yen ($2.48 billion) in the Bain Capital-led consortium that acquired Toshiba Memory, now Kioxia.

A Bain-managed investment vehicle completed the sale of all of its Kioxia shares in June, after Kioxia listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2024.

($1 = 159.0900 yen)

data.title: Greece projects faster 2027 growth, steeper debt ratio decline
data.description:
The government's final budget, before national elections in spring, projects economic growth to accelerate to 2.3% from 2.0% this year, with investments rising by 7.9% and private consumption by 1.5%.

• It projects a fiscal surplus of 0.1% of gross domestic product in 2027 and a primary surplus, which excludes interest-rate payments, of 3.2% of GDP.

• It also envisages a decline in debt-to-GDP ratio to 128.5% from 135.8% this year.

• The budget includes tax breaks and subsidies of about €2.2 billion ($2.41 billion) to boost low-income households and help pensioners who suffer from high energy and housing prices.

• The budget vote is expected in mid-December.

data.title: Gold slides toward worst week in eight months on hawkish Fed outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold slips for fifth session, hits lowest since September 2025
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for second weekly decline
  • Fed's Paulson says Fed will need to raise rates again
  • Physical gold demand in India and China picked up this week

By Sherin Sans

Gold extended its sharp selloff on Friday, hovering near a more than one-year low and heading for its steepest weekly decline in eight months, as expectations of a hawkish Federal Reserve boosted the dollar and Treasury yields.

Spot gold fell 1.3% to $3,576.09 per ounce by 0913 GMT, after touching its lowest level since September 4, 2025 at $3,513.54 earlier in the session. Bullion has shed about 8% this week, the most since the week ending March 20.

US gold futures for December delivery slid 2.9% to $3,577.60.

"Gold is under renewed pressure from hawkish Fed expectations, which are lifting real yields and the US dollar and raising the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. The ongoing AI-related equity sell-off is also prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses elsewhere," Critical Metals CEO Tony Sage said.

The selloff gathered pace after Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson joined other policymakers in flagging inflation risks that could warrant another interest-rate increase, reinforcing expectations that US borrowing costs will rise further.

Markets see a 99.3% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Asian shares tumbled on Friday and were headed for their worst week since 2020 after Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor confidence in the AI sector, while the dollar extended its rally on safe-haven demand.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in India and China strengthened this week as the price slump attracted bargain hunters, with investors in China viewing the correction as a buying opportunity.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.8% to $42.41, platinum dropped 2.3% to $1,313.20, and palladium slid 1.5% to $896.

All three metals are poised for second straight weekly declines.

"Silver, platinum and palladium are declining in tandem with gold primarily because of the same macro drivers. Silver is typically more volatile and has amplified the move this week. Platinum and palladium are also sensitive to growth concerns that accompany tighter monetary policy," Sage added.

data.title: Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Dominated Headlines This Week – AI Anxiety Eased, While Investors And Employees Reaped A Windfall
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic stock closed 17% higher on its first trading day, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $1.8 trillion.
  • Anthropic’s co-founders’ stakes were each valued at roughly $20 billion, while employees held about $232 billion in equity, or around $44 million per employee on average, according to Reuters. 
  • Nvidia topped Q3 expectations and said it does not plan to reinstate Huang as CEO.

Anthropic (ANT) dominated tech headlines this week with the largest IPO in history, while Nvidia (NVDA) also drew attention due to its earnings report.

Anthropic saw incredible demand for its IPO, and the stock popped on debut. Meanwhile, Nvidia reported another set of strong earnings even as the fallout from former CEO Jensen Huang’s departure continued to weigh on sentiment for the AI chipmakers.

Here’re the major developments from the week so far:

Anthropic Rises On Debut After Blockbuster IPO

ANT stock closed 17% higher on the first day, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $1.8 trillion. However, shares tumbled 6% in premarket trading on Friday, weighing on tech stocks. Analysts believe Anthropic’s growth, enterprise demand and model capabilities could drive further gains, though its heavy infrastructure costs and valuation remain key concerns.

About 68% of some 17,500 retail traders who voted in a Stocktwits poll said they had planned to avoid the stock on the debut day.

Anthropic Delivers Windfall For Investors, Employees

Anthropic’s IPO created enormous paper wealth. Its seven co-founders’ stakes were each valued at roughly $20 billion, while employees held about $232 billion in equity, or around $44 million per employee on average, according to Reuters.

Top investors Menlo Ventures, Spark Capital, and Lightspeed, among others, saw the value of their investment grow manyfold.

Nvidia Posts Another Record Quarter, Says No Plan To Reinstate Huang

Nvidia’s Q3 sales more than doubled to $115.8 billion, beating expectations, according to results issued on Tuesday. Revenue from the all-important data center segment rose 110% to $107.6 billion, also higher than targets.

The chipmaker raised its forecast revenue growth for fiscal 2028 from 70% to 75%.

Nvidia said it did not plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, who had earlier expressed a desire to return, and would continue the search for his replacement.

California Probes Nvidia

California opened an investigation into whether former CEO Jensen Huang’s actions allowed China to obtain advanced AI technology and misled investors, the state’s attorney general Rob Bonta announced on Thursday.

Meanwhile, lawmakers disclosed that the Commerce Department had approved sales of more than 800,000 advanced AI chips to Chinese firms through May, including companies on the Pentagon’s list of Chinese military firms.

The developments add to the Nvidia fallout as investors reassess their positions in a post-Huang era.

How Did Tech Stocks Move This Week?

Nebius (NBIS) and CoreWeave (CRWV) were the top tech losers in the Nasdaq-100 through Thursday, falling nearly 25% each. Palo Alto Networks (PANW) was the biggest gainer, up 12%.

The Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) lost 1.3%.

data.title: Japan's bank shares slide even as Ueda vows more rate rises
data.description:
Japanese bank shares fell on November 19 even as Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament that the central bank would keep raising interest rates.

The TOPIX Banks index opened 2.1% lower, Saxo Bank said, and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group , the country's biggest lender, opened 3.1% down. MUFG recovered to close 1.7% lower, its sixth straight daily fall. Mizuho Financial Group shed 2.1% and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group 0.8%, while the broader TOPIX ended flat and the Nikkei 225 gained 0.7%.

Ueda was presenting the central bank's twice-yearly report to the upper house's Committee on Financial Affairs. Underlying inflation 'is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent', he told the committee, and with financial conditions still accommodative 'the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation'. The policy rate has stood at 1.25% since September, up from minus 0.1% at the start of 2024.

Rising rates ought to be a windfall for lenders that spent a decade earning next to nothing on deposits. Japan's bank stocks, though, now trade less on where the policy rate is heading than on each lurch in the government bond market, and the past month has supplied several.

Bank of Japan policy rate and 10-year government bond yield, %, January 2024 to October 2026. Source: BIS, OECD via IntelliNews Lambda

Weak auction, strong auction

A day before Ueda spoke, the Ministry of Finance's sale of 20-year bonds drew bids of JPY1.91 trillion ($12.0bn) for the JPY525.8bn ($3.3bn) it accepted, a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.64. The October sale had attracted 5.84, the highest in the ministry's records going back to 1987, and the previous 12 auctions averaged 3.92. The tail, the gap between the average and lowest accepted prices, widened to 0.29 from 0.07.

Saxo Bank put the result down to 'reduced appetite for duration amid rising inflation expectations'.

A strong sale has hurt the banks as well. After October's record demand, bond futures rallied, long-term yields eased and the banking sub-index fell more than 3% that afternoon, Kabutan reported, as traders bet the climb in domestic rates might pause. Lenders treated by the market as rate plays are being sold when yields look set to stall and again when buyers of government debt hold back.

Bid-to-cover ratio at 20-year Japanese government bond auctions, January 2025 to November 18, 2026. Source: Ministry of Finance, Japan. IntelliNews

Paper losses and a leak

Valuation losses on yen-denominated bonds have been growing as rates climb, particularly at regional and shinkin banks with large holdings, the Bank of Japan said in its October Financial System Report. Word that the Financial Services Agency would examine shinkin banks' bond portfolios emerged in September, days after the 10-year yield touched 3% for the first time in three decades.

At MUFG, higher rates are already paying off. Its net interest income rose to JPY1.85 trillion ($11.6bn) in the six months to September from JPY1.44 trillion a year earlier, and net profit climbed 26.1% to JPY1.63 trillion ($10.2bn), its investor presentation shows. The group lifted its full-year profit target to JPY2.8 trillion ($17.5bn) from JPY2.7 trillion and added a buyback of up to JPY200bn ($1.25bn).

The paper loss on its JPY12.38 trillion ($77.4bn) of government bonds was a modest JPY0.13 trillion ($813mn). Its shares still fell 3.75% on November 17, the day it presented those numbers to investors.

MUFG Bank, the group's main lender, disclosed on November 18 that a breach at Plaid, a contractor whose KARTE service it uses for website and app messaging, had exposed the gender, age and home region of about 6.5mn customers, though not names or contact details. Nikkei tied the sixth consecutive fall in the shares to the leak. Japanese lenders were already tightening identity checks after a run of data breaches elsewhere.

The 160 line

The yen weakened past 160 per dollar on November 12 for the first time since early September, and the ECB's reference rates put it at 159.97 on November 19. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama told reporters on November 13 that the market was seeing rapid, one-sided moves and that Tokyo would keep working closely with the US Treasury and respond appropriately. The ministry bought JPY15.4 trillion ($96.3bn) of yen between July 30 and August 3, its intervention records show.

A cheap yen feeds the inflation Ueda wants to pin down. data.title: RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RLX Technology Inc. ("RLX Technology" or the "Company") (), a leading global branded e-vapor company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Gross profit increased by 26.7% to RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.
  • Non-GAAP income from operations[1] was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP net income[1] was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

"The third quarter marked a defining inflection point for RLX as we integrated our newly acquired European distribution platform with our existing retail footprint, evolving into a leading global smoke-free brand," said Ms. Ying (Kate) Wang, Co-founder, Chairperson, and Chief Executive Officer of RLX Technology. "We now possess end-to-end capabilities spanning global product innovation, supply chain execution, and direct route-to-market reach, while always placing our brands at the heart of adult consumers' choices worldwide. By pairing these strengths with dedicated local field teams and an open, multi-brand ecosystem philosophy, we are gaining sharper retail insights that will empower us to tailor products to local consumer preferences, scale our multi-category portfolio, and capture market share as shifting global regulations reshape the industry."

Mr. Chao Lu, Chief Financial Officer of RLX Technology, commented, "We delivered strong third quarter financial results, with the consolidation driving a surge in net revenues to RMB1.92 billion, up 69.7% year over year. International markets contributed 86.5% of our top line. While our blended gross margin now reflects the consolidation of the distribution business, we maintained solid non-GAAP profitability, improved working capital efficiency, and achieved a healthy sequential rebound in operating cash flow. Looking ahead, we are actively lifting our European platform's margins through supply chain optimization and capital deployment, while navigating transitional working capital needs related to the UK's October introduction of an excise duty. Supported by RMB13.48 billion in total financial assets, we have the financial flexibility to fund global brand expansion, deliver long-term sustainable growth, and maintain strong shareholder returns."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity in July 2026. Net revenues from international business represented 86.5% of net revenues for the period.

Gross profit was RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 26.7% from RMB352.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.

Operating expenses were RMB407.1 million (US$60.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB259.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and increased shipping and logistics costs.

Selling expenses were RMB182.9 million (US$27.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB132.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increases in salary and welfare expenses and shipping and logistics costs.

General and administrative expenses were RMB185.9 million (US$27.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and legal and other consulting fees.

Research and development expenses were RMB38.3 million (US$5.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB41.3 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP income from operations was RMB39.5 million (US$5.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB93.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Income tax expense was RMB43.6 million (US$6.5 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB45.9 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP net income was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") were RMB0.131 (US$0.020) and RMB0.123 (US$0.018), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.167 and RMB0.157, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS[2] were RMB0.186 (US$0.028) and RMB0.175 (US$0.026), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.236 and RMB0.221, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

Hacksaw Gaming is pleased to announce its entry into Delaware. The company is launching an initial selection of its acclaimed slot portfolio with BetRivers, an online casino brand of Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI). The launch brings Hacksaw titles to players in the state for the first time and marks another milestone in the company’s US expansion.

In October 2026, Hacksaw Gaming obtained approval as a Gaming Vendor from the Delaware Lottery. This paved the way for its entry into the locally licensed market through BetRivers, which operates online gaming in Delaware on behalf of the Delaware Lottery.

Philippa Gregory, Operational CEO of Hacksaw Gaming, commented:

“Going live in Delaware with BetRivers is a fantastic milestone for Hacksaw Gaming and another important step in our US expansion. RSI was our very first partner in the US, and we’ve built a great relationship with the team over the years. Building on our successful launches together in West Virginia and New Jersey, we’re delighted to be bringing our games to players in Delaware and continuing to grow our presence across the US.”

The launch adds Delaware to Hacksaw Gaming’s growing network of locally licensed US markets, which now includes six states: Connecticut, Delaware, Michigan, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and West Virginia.

For more information, please contact:

E-mail: ir@hacksawgroup.com

About Hacksaw

Hacksaw AB (publ) is a B2B technology platform and game development company. The scalable and modular platform, built on a modern code base, enables rapid development and distribution of games. Games developed by Hacksaw comprise digital slots, scratch cards, crash games and prediction market infrastructure solutions designed for gaming operators and other qualified businesses. We operate across the whole B2B iGaming value chain, from game development to distribution and our customers comprise some of the largest private and state-owned iGaming operators in the industry. data.title: Anthropic shares slip after rallying in record-breaking IPO debut
data.description:
Anthropic shares fell in their second day of trading as a broader market selloff and growing concerns over the AI trade weighed on sentiment following the stock’s record-setting debut.

The company’s shares fell as much as 7.4% in early premarket trading Friday, a day after surging 17% in their public market debut. The stock traded as low as $90 as of 4:02 a.m. in New York, compared with Thursday's closing price of $97.17. Shares remained above the IPO price of $83.

The decline came amid broader market weakness, with Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.9%. The initial surge reflected strong investor demand for the heavily oversubscribed IPO, but the company's steep valuation and fresh competitive threats weighed on shares Friday as investors broadly pulled back from riskier assets.

Anthropic’s $107.3B IPO attracted global demand for seven times the shares on offer. Competition was so intense that more than half of institutional investors bidding for shares received no allocation, Bloomberg reported Thursday. The IPO surpassed the previous record set by SpaceX in June, which raised a total of $86.25B, including additional shares sold by underwriters through the overallotment option.

Goldman Sachs Group , Morgan Stanley , and 20 other banks earned a record $550M in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.
